chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not enter the bathhouse except with a loincloth.'

key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: The bathhouse, a public place for ritual and physical bathing
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ: The Last Day, referring to the Day of Judgment
key_terms.بِمِئْزَرٍ: With a loincloth or waist-wrapper, used for modesty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on entering the bathhouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish the etiquette of 'haya' (modesty) within the communal bathhouses prevalent in early Islamic society. The Prophet’s instruction to wear a mi'zar (loincloth) underscores that physical modesty is an outward manifestation of inner faith, ensuring that the body is covered appropriately even in spaces of cleansing. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining dignity and decorum in daily social interactions as a reflection of one's spiritual state.
